samples.summary: Clipboard buffer lifetime extended indefinitely: copied cell values, formulas, styles and merge layout now persist in memory until Escape
samples.evidence: Both view paste paths drop their `clearCopyBuffer()` call (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4947 and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:728). `Sheet.copyBuffer` holds a full snapshot of the copied region — `grid` (raw cell values AND formulas), `rangeStyles`, `text`, and now `merges` (sheet.ts:2155). Previously that snapshot of potentially sensitive spreadsheet content was discarded after a single paste; it now lives for the whole life of the `Sheet` instance, cleared only by the Escape keybinding (view/worksheet.ts:5117-5118) or `clearCopyBuffer()`, which now has exactly one caller. There is no clear on blur, on window unload, on tab/document teardown, or on losing edit permission. An attacker with later access to the page context (a same-origin XSS elsewhere in the app, a heap/memory dump, or a devtools-capable observer on a shared machine) reads copied confidential cell data that would previously have been released. Impact is bounded — it is the user's own data in their own tab, and the OS clipboard retains the TSV anyway — so this is hardening, not an exploit. Suggest clearing the buffer on sheet teardown/detach as well as on Escape.

samples.summary: Internal-paste detection is plaintext equality against a now long-lived buffer, so foreign clipboard content matching the copied text is substituted with the retained internal grid
samples.evidence: `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2243) is the only check distinguishing a trusted internal paste from untrusted external clipboard data. On the internal branch the pasted content is taken from `this.copyBuffer.grid` — including formulas — and `applyInputInferenceToGrid` (the conservative sanitising/inference pass applied to external TSV/HTML at sheet.ts:2300-2302) is deliberately skipped. Because the buffer is no longer cleared after each paste, this trust decision now applies for the buffer's entire lifetime rather than for one paste. An attacker who can get the victim to copy a known string (e.g. a value displayed on an attacker page, or by seeding the OS clipboard from a page with clipboard-write) and paste it can cause the editor to write the retained internal grid — formulas, styles and merge blocks — instead of the literal text the user believes they are pasting. No code-execution primitive exists (no eval/fetch in packages/sheets), so impact is data integrity/spoofing only, and the equality check itself predates this change; the change widens its window. A stronger discriminator (e.g. a nonce embedded in the internal HTML flavour) would remove the ambiguity.

samples.summary: `Worksheet.paste()` has no internal read-only guard, unlike the adjacent `cut()`; enforcement lives solely at its one keybinding call site
samples.evidence: `Worksheet.cut()` self-guards with `if (this.readOnly) return;` (view/worksheet.ts:4908), but `Worksheet.paste()` (view/worksheet.ts:4914) — the method this change edits — has no such guard. The only thing preventing a read-only viewer from writing through it is the keybinding handler at view/worksheet.ts:5141 (`if (this.readOnly) return;`). I enumerated the call sites: `this.paste()` is invoked only from that handler inside packages/sheets, and the frontend context menu path (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:776) goes through `Spreadsheet.paste()`, which does check `this._readOnly` (view/spreadsheet.ts:699), so I could NOT complete an exploit chain today. The weakness is that the write path is unguarded at the point that performs the write, so any future caller (mobile handle, context menu wired to the Worksheet, an API method) silently bypasses read-only. `Sheet.paste()` itself likewise has no permission concept — only `if (this.pivotDefinition) return;` (sheet.ts:2217). Adding `if (this.readOnly) return;` to `Worksheet.paste()` mirrors `cut()` and makes the gate unbypassable by construction.

samples.summary: Local merge cache is mutated regardless of whether the store persisted the write; `ReadonlyStore.deleteMerge` returns false and the result is ignored
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges` does `await this.store.deleteMerge(merge.anchor); this.merges.delete(anchorSref);` (sheet.ts:2538-2539) and `await this.store.setMerge(...); this.merges.set(...)` (sheet.ts:2543-2544), never inspecting the outcome. `ReadonlyStore.setMerge` is a silent no-op and `ReadonlyStore.deleteMerge` returns `false` (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:272-278). So if `Sheet.paste` is ever reached with a read-only store — the model layer enforces no permission of its own — the in-memory merge map, `mergeCoverMap` and the rendered layout diverge from the authoritative store, showing a viewer a mutation that was never persisted. Persisted state is safe (the store is the enforcement point) and the view-layer gates currently keep this unreachable, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a bypass; the same ignore-the-result pattern already exists at sheet.ts:4765 in `unmergeSelection`. Checking the store result (or having ReadonlyStore reject rather than no-op) would make the failure loud.

samples.summary: Merge spans are never validated on load, and the paste path now adds a fresh O(rs*cs) awaited-store-read loop driven by them (resource exhaustion from untrusted merge metadata)
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges` calls `clearCellsUnderMerge` per pasted block (sheet.ts:2545), which iterates `mergeCoveredSrefs(anchor, span)` — an rs*cs loop — performing `await this.store.get(ref)` for every covered cell (sheet.ts:2564+). The spans come from `this.merges`, populated by `loadMerges()` (sheet.ts:544-547) straight from `store.getMerges()` with no bound on `rs`/`cs`; I found no validation of span magnitude anywhere in packages/sheets/src/store or in the loaders. Merge metadata can originate from a remote collaborator's document state or an imported XLSX (the task doc itself notes the XLSX importer accepts blocks it should not), i.e. from input the client does not control. A hostile span therefore turns a single paste into an effectively unbounded awaited loop, hanging the tab. Confidence is low because the primary enabler is out of this diff — `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:818-830) already materialises rs*cs entries at load time, so such a document wedges the client before any paste — and because `clearCellsUnderMerge` is relocated rather than newly written code. The paste path is nonetheless a new way to reach it. A sanity bound on `rs`/`cs` at load would close the class.
